parts.note: On the Mac, in your own (admin) account's Terminal: the only step that needs an admin. Paste it as it is; sysadminctl asks for the new user's password, which you keep (agents never get it). A Mac nobody else uses is best: then there's no Apple ID or browser login on it at all.
parts.title: In your own account: make the agents' user

values.label: In your own account's Terminal
values.note: Each line says why. It never pipes anything from the network into sudo.
values.value:
# A standard (non-admin) user of its own for agents. You choose its password and keep it.
sudo sysadminctl -addUser agents -fullName "fleetd agents" -password -
# Simulators and debugging for that user, with no admin prompt.
sudo dseditgroup -o edit -a agents -t user _developer
sudo DevToolsSecurity -enable
# Xcode's licence and its system components, which only an admin can accept and install.
sudo xcodebuild -license accept && sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
# Your own home closed to every other user, agents included.
chmod 700 ~

parts.note: Log out (or switch user) and log in as fleetd agents, then paste the join line in its Terminal. It refuses an admin user, installs fleetd for that user only, and joins as the agents' Mac: a tool every project's agents use, which runs no claude and no Navi and takes no secret. Settings › Hub › Machines › Add machine › A Mac for agents makes the line with its one-time code.
parts.title: Log in as fleetd agents and join

values.label: In fleetd agents' Terminal
values.note: Or on the hub: fleetd pair --worker mac, then add --mac to the line it prints.

parts.note: Still logged in as fleetd agents: turn on fleetd in Accessibility and in Screen Recording, so agents can drive the Mac's apps and you can watch them. macOS may ask for an administrator's name and password: type yours in that System Settings dialog at the Mac itself, never through fleetd's view of its screen. Then restart its node (launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/sh.fleetd.node): macOS gives a running process a new grant only once it starts again. It asks again from time to time; the check says when.
parts.title: Two clicks at the Mac

values.label: Accessibility, at the Mac
values.note: In fleetd agents' Terminal: it opens the pane. Turn on fleetd there.

parts.note: First let the agents running on it finish (or stop them), and push any work they left: removing the old node deletes its worktrees. Join it again from fleetd agents with the same name and --rejoin (Add machine offers the line), so its history stays. Then, in your own account, stop and remove its old node: your account runs no fleetd node after. The rejoin gave the Mac a new key, so the old node would be refused anyway.
